- Diversified and de-risked business operations with a large and growing total addressable market - active business lines in Copper, Barite, Fluorspar and Edible Oil, with operational hubs in India, Morocco and Singapore and customers across 5 countries (fiscal 2025 and nine months ended December 2025), spanning Asia, the Middle East, Europe, Africa, South America and North America
- Curated commodity mix intended to build sustainable, de-risked and counter-cyclical cash flows designed to withstand market volatility and capitalize on region-specific demand cycles
- Years of operational expertise across each commodity - active in the edible oil segment since 1996 and diversified into the global Barite, Fluorspar and Copper markets since 2015
- Operational hubs strategically located to optimize supply chain efficiency and market proximity - Barite operations anchored in Morocco and India, both ranked among the world's top three Barite producers
- Morocco logistics advantage - use of both the Port of Casablanca and the Port of Agadir for bulk and container shipments, giving cost-efficient access to Europe, Africa, the Americas and the Middle East; Morocco is the third-largest Barite producer globally
- India Barite operations located in Andhra Pradesh, home to India's largest and the world's single largest Barite mine, and just 128 km from Krishnapatnam Port
- Rice bran oil business based in Andhra Pradesh, the fourth-largest rice-producing state in India (the world's largest rice producer), with rice bran sourced from local rice mills, other rice-producing regions and trusted traders; abundant bran availability plus infrastructure enables aggressive pricing of finished products
- Promoters actively involved in all critical aspects of the business including product innovation, sales and marketing, finance, operations, strategy and quality
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Extreme dependence on subsidiaries for revenue — The RHP's first risk factor states that 87.85%, 77.27%, 81.30% and 70.24% of consolidated revenue for the period ended December 31, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 respectively came from subsidiaries; any loss of sales due to reduced demand for the subsidiaries' products would have a material adverse effect on business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. (Note: the FY2025 and FY2024 percentages in this risk-factor heading, 77.27% and 81.30%, do not reconcile with the 86.11% and 81.85% shown in the table immediately below it in the same risk factor.)
- Concentration in a narrow set of minerals - Barite, Fluorspar and Copper Cathode — The Company states it relies heavily on revenue generated from the sale of Barite, Fluorspar, Copper Cathode and other minerals, so any reduction in demand for these products directly hits results.
- Exposure to a downturn in the rice bran oil industry — Explicitly flagged twice in risk factor 1 - a downturn in the rice bran oil industry may adversely impact business, results of operations and financial condition.
- Inability to scale operations, retain existing customers or expand the customer base — The RHP states success depends on the ability to diversify and grow operations and retain/expand customers for Barite, Fluorspar, Copper Cathode and other minerals; failure would cause revenue from operations and cash flow to decline, and there is no assurance such a decline will not occur.
- Export/geographic concentration outside India — 86.11% of consolidated revenue in fiscal 2025 and 87.85% in the nine months ended December 31, 2025 came from outside India (UAE, Singapore, Oman, Germany, Suriname, USA), with the country mix shifting sharply between periods - UAE went from 35.75% of revenue in FY2025 to nil in the nine-month period.
- Morocco Barite mining licence is not yet in hand — Only a mining permit (No. 3739267) has been allocated; the Company expects the mining licence by end June 2026 or mid-July 2026, and commercial extraction and sale of barite is only proposed to commence thereafter - so the backward-integration benefit is contingent on a pending regulatory approval.
- Copper procurement depends on third-party trading partners for Chile-origin material — Copper cathodes are sourced from smelters in Chile with procurement diversified through multiple trading partners across Singapore and the UAE - the Company does not own the smelting source, and copper was 54.72% of fiscal 2025 consolidated revenue.
- Leverage remains material despite improvement — Net Debt/EBITDA was 5.67 in FY2023 and 5.09 in FY2024, improving to 1.68 in FY2025 and 1.63 for the nine months ended December 31, 2025; Rs. 1,000 lakhs of Net Proceeds is earmarked for prepayment/repayment of certain loans.

business.body: Sri Priyanka Geo Commex Limited supplies minerals - Barite, Fluorspar and Copper Cathode - to industries spanning energy, chemicals, infrastructure and electronics, with the India Barite/Fluorspar business run by the Company and the international business run through its Singapore subsidiary Geo Min Commodities Pte. Ltd and its Morocco step-down subsidiary Atlas Resources International. In parallel it operates across the rice bran oil value chain, manufacturing crude rice bran oil, refining it and processing the associated residues and by-products (DORB, fatty acids, gums, spent earth and wax) at an Andhra Pradesh facility. Rice bran oil is sold mainly in bulk to players who sell edible oil in unbranded or loose form and to re-packers; Barite and Fluorspar are supplied to customers in the United States, Germany, Suriname and Oman, and Grade A copper cathodes to customers in the UAE and Singapore.

outlook.body: The principal stated expansion is backward integration into mining in Morocco to secure supply for the Barite and Copper businesses: the Company has secured mining permits for one Barite mine and one Copper mine, both in Morocco. The Barite permit (Permit No. 3739267) covers an area in the Ighoud Commune, Youssoufia Province, Marrakech-Safi Region, Kingdom of Morocco, which per geological assessment reports is estimated to contain approximately 0.75 million MT of Barite ore at an average grade of 4.25. The Company expects to receive the mining licence by the end of June 2026 or mid-July 2026, following which commercial extraction and sale of barite from the mine is proposed to commence; no timeline is stated for the Copper mine. Separately, in fiscal 2025 and the nine months ended December 2025 the Company expanded into domestic Barite trading in India, with operations located in Andhra Pradesh (home to India's largest and the world's single largest Barite mine) 128 km from Krishnapatnam Port, serving both domestic and international markets. No expansion of the existing 60,000 MT per annum solvent extraction plant or 15,000 MT per annum oil refinery is stated in the routed text.

outlook.body:
- Revenue is overwhelmingly subsidiary-driven: subsidiaries contributed 87.85% of consolidated revenue for the nine months ended December 31, 2025 and 86.11% in fiscal 2025, versus 70.24% in fiscal 2023
- Copper Cathode described as a key revenue driver offering a scalable and consistent revenue stream, portfolio diversification and strong international linkages
- Commodity mix shift between periods: Copper fell from 54.72% of consolidated revenue in fiscal 2025 to 44.39% in the nine months ended December 2025 while Barite/Fluorspar rose from 21.95% to 29.18%
- Geographic mix shift: UAE (35.75% of revenue in fiscal 2025) recorded nil revenue in the nine months ended December 2025 while the USA (nil in fiscal 2025) contributed Rs. 6,273.20 lakhs (25.26%) and Singapore rose to Rs. 14,529.66 lakhs (58.50%)
- Barite volumes stepped up sharply while Fluorspar volumes fell - Barite sales of 35,672.26 tons in FY2025 versus 70,730.76 tons in the nine months ended December 31, 2025; Fluorspar 15,163.22 tons versus 4,066 tons
- Stated margin trajectory: EBITDA margin of 1.86% (FY2023), 2.42% (FY2024), 6.18% (FY2025) and 10.53% (nine months ended December 31, 2025); PAT margin 0.61%, 0.81%, 3.69% and 7.15% over the same periods
- Stated leverage trajectory: Net Debt/EBITDA of 5.67 (FY2023), 5.09 (FY2024), 1.68 (FY2025) and 1.63 (nine months ended December 31, 2025)
- Asset-light IT and operations profile: no specialised, proprietary or custom-built software; standard off-the-shelf accounting software and basic IT tools only
- Rice bran sourced locally from Andhra Pradesh rice mills and traders, with proximity to ports and road infrastructure cited as reducing procurement and logistics costs

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration: the Group has secured mining permits for one Barite mine and one Copper mine, both in Morocco, stated to secure supplies at low mining cost and de-risk the business from price shocks. The Barite mining permit (No. 3739267, Ighoud Commune, Youssoufia Province, Marrakech-Safi Region, Morocco) covers an area estimated on geological assessment reports to contain approximately 0.75 million MT of Barite ore at an average grade of 4.25; the mining licence is expected by end-June 2026 or mid-July 2026, after which commercial extraction and sale are proposed to commence. The planned copper mining operations, supported by an on-site flotation unit, are intended to enable copper cathode production via third-party smelters. Pending own mining, procurement is anchored by the Morocco subsidiary Atlas Resources International, which buys Barite and Fluorspar from Moroccan miners under long-term supply agreements: (i) agreement dated January 1, 2022 for purchase of Mixed Barite Fluorspar, valid till December 30, 2028, and (ii) agreement dated January 1, 2023 for purchase of Drilling Grade Barite 4.20 density API Grade, valid till December 30, 2027. Atlas has executed 100% of its sales to the Company and to Geo Min Commodities Pte. Ltd., Singapore, which procures all Atlas-sourced material and markets it in USA, Germany, Singapore, UAE, Oman and Suriname; Copper Cathode is procured from Chile through multiple trading partners across Singapore and the UAE. The Atlas-procurement / Geo Min-marketing structure is stated to be designed to take advantage of different tax rates in Morocco and Singapore and to keep ultimate-buyer details within the Singapore entity. In India, the Company began trading Barite in FY2025 and is eligible to participate in Andhra Pradesh Mineral Development Corporation (APMDC) tenders (prior transaction experience being a mandatory requirement), with operations located 128 km from Krishnapatnam Port; the RHP states such tenders are open to other participants and may or may not be awarded to the Company. Forward integration: for drilling-grade barite serving oil & gas, the Company plans to install its own grinding mills to deliver product from its mines directly to oil rigs; for industrial-grade barite it plans milling, beneficiation and leaching plants to achieve barite sulphate purities of 96-97%. In rice bran oil, the Company plans to sell a portion of refined oil under its own brand, creating a direct-to-consumer brand. Logistics: Port of Casablanca and Port of Agadir in Morocco for bulk and container shipments; planned investment in warehousing and port-based logistics support via the Singapore and Morocco subsidiaries; mineral testing/quality certification outsourced to Mitra S. K. Morocco SARL.

overview.business_model: Two revenue streams. (1) Minerals: the Company sells Barite and Fluorspar in India, while the international mineral business runs through wholly-owned subsidiary Geo Min Commodities Pte. Ltd. (Singapore), which acts as the global marketing and selling arm, and its step-down subsidiary Atlas Resources International (Morocco), which acts as the procurement arm; customers are in the United States, Germany, Suriname and Oman, serving oil & gas and chemical industries. Geo Min's operation is stated to be highly dependent on Copper Cathode sourced from a few key suppliers with no long-term supply agreements. (2) Rice bran oil: the Company extracts crude rice bran oil and refines it, plus sells associated residues and by-products (De-Oiled Rice Bran, Fatty Acids, Gums, Spent Earth and Wax), selling mainly in bulk to players who sell edible oil in unbranded/loose form and to re-packers. Stated installed capacity is 60,000 MT per annum solvent extraction and 15,000 MT per annum oil refinery as on the date of the RHP. red_flags: Operating cash outflow of Rs (1,059.78) lakhs for the nine months ended December 31, 2025 - the largest in the series - recorded against the largest PAT (Rs 1,775.75 lakhs), alongside unsecured third-party loans of Rs 2,105.99 lakhs that 'may be recalled at any time' and a Rs 402.11 lakh long-term borrowing line that is entirely promoter/family lending. Cash cover for a recall is Rs 1,061.65 lakhs of cash and bank balances, of which Rs 233.36 lakhs is margin/collateral fixed deposits.

The Copper Cathode supplier table is arithmetically impossible as printed: FY2023 Supplier 1 at Rs 6,387.55 lakhs = 29.76% of purchases against Supplier 2 at Rs 3,544.43 lakhs = 70.24% - a larger amount at the smaller percentage, and both percentages are identical to the Sri Priyanka / Subsidiaries revenue split (29.76% / 70.24%) in the table immediately above, indicating a column carried over from the wrong table. Separately, FY2025 shows Supplier 1 at Rs 14,237.61 lakhs = '100%' of purchases while the top-one-supplier row for the same year shows Rs 16,301.63 lakhs = 72.74%; the two cannot both hold.

Impossible date sequence in the audit trail: paragraph 5 of the Examination Report dates the FY2024 statutory audit report 16 August 2024, while paragraph 4(c) states the FY2024 Consolidated Financial Statements were approved by the Board on 17 August 2024 - the audit report is dated one day before the statements it reports on were adopted.

The same related-party lease is printed with two irreconcilable execution dates and a forward commencement: the RPT disclosure dates the rent agreement with Promoter Venkata Sai Shiv Prasad Nuthalapati June 11, 2025 while the leased-premises table dates it May 9, 2026, with an eleven-month term stated to run w.e.f. May 13, 2026 - weeks before the RHP date of June 18, 2026 in one reading and roughly eleven months after execution in the other.
